jobs.name: todo-digest
jobs.prompt: Trigger the morning to-do digest. POST to https://custom-to-do-app-production.up.railway.app/api/organize?unprocessedOnly=true (no body needed). The endpoint classifies unprocessed items with Claude and posts a Block Kit digest to Slack #brain-dump itself — partitioned with #top items under a 🔴 Priority header, others under 📋 Other new items. After the request returns, check the JSON in this order: (1) if HTTP status != 200, reply 'Digest endpoint error: <status>'. (2) Else if a `slack` array exists and any entry has ok !== true, reply 'Digest classified N items but Slack post failed: <error codes from failing entries>' — this means #brain-dump never got the post. (3) Otherwise reply with the `message` field (e.g. '5 new items captured' or 'No new ideas since last organize'). Under 40 words. Atlas voice — no hype.

jobs.name: code-standup
jobs.prompt: Post a morning code standup to Slack #chief. Pull source data live from GitHub via the github MCP — Erik's username is `eriksilver`. Steps: (1) Call mcp_github_search_repositories with `user:eriksilver` to enumerate his repos. (2) For each repo, call mcp_github_list_commits with `since` set to yesterday 00:00 Central (US/Chicago) and `until` set to today 00:00 Central — skip repos with no commits in that window. (3) Format the post: one-line greeting → `Yesterday:` (group by repo, one-line per commit, leading bullet, short subject only, skip merge commits) → `Queued / planned:` (pull from todo-app `mcp_todo_app_list_dev_projects` where status is `active`; if none active, say `Nothing queued.`) → one dry one-line observation about momentum or focus. Under 250 words. Atlas voice — no hype, no apology, no emoji.
